verdict.rationale: Clerk's CLI docs say `clerk deploy` helps configure OAuth providers, and its Enterprise SSO supports SAML and OIDC identity providers such as Azure AD, Okta and Google Workspace. That shows configuration-driven external IdP sign-in. However, the pack never lists a broad catalog of social providers (e.g., GitHub, Apple, Facebook) or documents dashboard-only toggling of social connections. Missing for 10: a documented catalog of supported social/OAuth providers, first-party docs showing configuration-only (no-code) enablement of social connections, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can offer sign-in with a broad set of social and OAuth identity providers through configuration, not custom code

citations.quote: Clerk helps you set up your domain, OAuth providers, and DNS records with confidence.
Enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) allows users to sign in seamlessly using their Identity Provider (IdP) credentials (e.g.,Azure AD, Okta, or Google Workspace)
Clerk supports multiple protocols for implementing Enterprise SSO, including SAML and OIDC.
